articles.title: Scrap 2027 tax rise to help private rental sector – call
articles.summary: Official data shows the rate of increase in private rents has halved over the past year – prompting a call for a tax U-turn by the government. According to the Office for National Statistics (ONS), average monthly private rents across the UK increased by 3.3% in the 12 months to May this year.  This was […]
articles.ai_summary:
- Average private rents in the UK rose by 3.3% over the past year, marking a slowdown in rental price growth.  
- Experts urge the government to reverse the planned 2027 tax hike to support the struggling private rental sector.

articles.title: Flurry of new mortgage products and reduced rates for landlords
articles.summary: Competition hots up for landlord borrowers
articles.ai_summary:

- Competitive rates are being slashed, intensifying the appeal for landlord borrowers amid robust market competition.

articles.title: Nightmare for landlords trying to sell flats
articles.summary: New analysis by Zoopla shows the gap between house and flat prices across the UK is the widest it has been in 30 years – since records began.  The average price of a house is up 43% since 2016 across the UK, but flats have increased by just 10% over the same period.  As such, […]
articles.ai_summary:
- The price gap between houses and flats in the UK has reached its widest point in 30 years, with houses seeing a 43% increase since 2016 while flats lag behind at just 10%.  
- Landlords aiming to sell flats are facing significant challenges due to this historic disparity in property value growth.

articles.title: So why do landlords hold back deposits from tenants?
articles.summary: The DPS has set out the major reasons why landlords keep deposits from tenants
articles.ai_summary:
- **Common Reasons for Withholding Deposits**: The Deposit Protection Service (DPS) highlights that landlords often retain deposits due to damages, unpaid rent, or tenant breaches of the lease agreement.  
- **Impact on Tenants**: Such practices can significantly affect tenants financially, leading to disputes and increased tension in landlord-tenant relationships.

articles.title: Police called to landlord-tenant dispute make amazing discovery
articles.summary: Police officers in Greater Manchester were called to a landlord-tenant dispute that got out of hand – and made an amazing discovery. During the visit, officers identified a large quantity of goods stored on site, including a substantial number of vapes. Bolton council trading standards teams attended to assess the legitimacy of the products and […]
articles.ai_summary:
- Police addressing a landlord-tenant dispute in Greater Manchester stumbled upon a massive cache of goods, particularly a significant amount of vapes.  
- Bolton council's trading standards team is investigating the legitimacy of these products following the discovery.

articles.title: Private renting – how has it changed since Brexit referendum?
articles.summary: As we approach the 10th anniversary of the Brexit referendum, a new analysis looks at private rental sector changes since 2016. During that time Britain’s private rented sector (PRS) has grown by an estimated 6.6% from 2.98m rental properties to 3.17m. Regional variations The overall increase in stock has been driven by England, where the […]
articles.ai_summary:
- The UK's private rented sector has expanded by 6.6% since the Brexit referendum, rising from 2.98 million to 3.17 million rental properties.  
- This growth is primarily fueled by increasing stock in England, highlighting significant regional variations in the rental market.

articles.title: Landlords borrow more to fund EPC improvements
articles.summary: The data comes from Paragon Bank
articles.ai_summary:
- UK landlords are increasingly borrowing funds to enhance property energy performance certificates (EPCs), signaling a shift towards more sustainable housing.  
- Paragon Bank reports a rise in financing activity as landlords invest in upgrades to meet regulatory standards and improve tenant appeal.

articles.title: Burnham’s Manchester named ‘UK’s top capital appreciation city’
articles.summary: Manchester is the fastest growing city for prices over the last 10 years, while London is the slowest.
articles.ai_summary:

- In contrast, London is lagging behind, showing the slowest rate of property price increase during the same period.
